newsitem.title: FRANCE: Slain Frenchman did not want to carry the can.
newsitem.headline: Slain Frenchman did not want to carry the can.

text.p: A French businessman slain in Kinshasa said 24 hours before his death that he did not want to carry the can for Paris' years of support for the rule of Mobutu Sese Seko.

"I go around the town a lot. I run a business and I've already been stopped at cross-roads and called 'French bastard' and so on," Michel Tournaire, one of two Frenchmen killed in Kinshasa on Tuesday, told Radio Monte Carlo radio in an interview recorded on Monday afternoon.
"We bear no grudges... I would say this is a legitimate reaction from the population. These people have suffered 30 years of one-party rule and our government backed the rulers for years," he said.
Tournaire and Herve Rigaud, both long-time residents of Kinshasa, were shot dead by men in uniform as they left a factory in the city's Western Limete district around 7 p.m. on Tuesday.

Residents say anti-French feeling has swept Kinshasa since it became clear that Mobutu's 32-year rule would be brought to an end by the rebel forces of Laurent Kabila, who has declared himself president of the renamed Democratic Republic of Congo.
"We do not see why we should carry the can for this policy which we ceased supporting years ago," Tournaire had said in the radio interview.

France "never asked us what we thought and I think we are going to let it be known," he said, adding French businessmen in Kinshasa were setting up associations to tell the new rulers that they were not representatives of the French government.
The interview was re-broadcast on Wednesday by Radio France Internationale.
